frontier.hypothesis: Narrowing sin_p/cos_p's live range (dereferencing into fresh scalars immediately after computation, before the first func_80053614 call, instead of re-dereferencing the pointers in the post-call if(flags!=0) adjustment) may reduce register pressure enough to flip reload's spill-vs-keep decision for pseudo 149 (the 0x1F8002B8 literal, confirmed via s24's .greg read to be homed in $fp across the whole loop body).
frontier.mechanism: reload1.c's alter_reg spill-vs-keep decision is a global cost/pressure tradeoff across all pseudos live at a given point; shrinking a competing pseudo's (sin_p/cos_p) live range reduces 149's effective conflict pressure without touching 149's own live range directly.
frontier.next_probe: Apply the sin_p/cos_p-narrowing change on the current 38/198 chassis, measure via sandbox func_80056CB8 --disable all, then re-run pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 and read the fresh .greg dump to directly verify whether pseudo 149's disposition (hard-reg-resident vs stack-spilled) actually changed, not just re-measure the aggregate sandbox score blind. This is the ledger's highest-value untried lever since s24 named it.
